sections.text: Introduction

This document outlines maintenance procedure P1, 
to be performed after 1500 operations indicated in the title block.
The first draft initiated by eng 
Mohamed Aly Aly Hassan, El_Shabab Gas Turbine
Power Station and tested 
at 11 April 2002
Safety Precautions

items:
A work permit must be issued, the qualified maintenance staff should carry the suitable safety 
category,

Safety fence (rope) with caution 
marks surrounding the work area,
Switch off, the CB and disconnect switches on both sides. (busbar and line)

Block the CB drive and
disconnect switch on busbar, and on line side

Switch off the control voltage 125v, and effectively grounded before work on the 
CB

sections.text: Work to be carried out
Clean the condition of the winding motor and replace brushes.
Check the correct operation of safety devices.
Check the hydraulic oil level is normal +6 mm
Check the correct operation of operating coils and aux. switch.
Replace any damaged or warm parts.
Check the source voltage control value.

Check the
 operation of the circuit from
 manual position.

Check the
 operation of the circuit from
 remote
 position.
Check any gas leaks.
Check the gas density relay insulating gas.
Check the gas pressure 6 bar abs at 20 degree Centigrade.

Measure
 the closing
 time of the CB < 50 ms

Measure the tripping time of the 
 CB < 60 ms
Check the operating mechanism
Check the DC resistance.

Important

The
 most accurate test results will always be obtained at close to atmospheric
 pressure, a pressure reducing device should be used when testing SF6 gas under
 system pressure, Sampling lines must be clean an dry, the lines and instrument
 must be purged for several minutes with the gas to be tested before the actual
 test is carried out.
Test Setup

rows:
1. SF6
 gas cylinder or switchgear compartment

items:
Adjust the pressure reducing valve at the sampling point to
 approximately 1 bar above atmosphericpressure. Install the flowmeter on top
 of the instrument , connect the sample gas line starting from thesampling
 point to the Gas In connection on the instrument. Make sure that all
 connections are tight and that all valves are closed .

Open the main valve of cylinder or gas compartment
 slightly Open flowmeter valve (8) completely, open control valve (5)
 slightly until the flowmeter indicatesa gas flow through the instrument of
 30 L/H.

Press Mains switch, the button should be illuminated . Set
 Mode switch to Measurement, the button is in the released position. The
 indicator needle will first remain in the No Dew position ( red field
 ). After a short time it will move into the green field (Correct position)
 and remain there. This indicates that the cooling capacity is sufficient and
 the instrument will correctly display the dew point. If the indicator needle
 remains inside the red field, the effective dew point lies below the cooling
 capacity of the instrument.

sections.text: Notes

Observe the digital read-out until it has stabilized, this
can sometimes take a considerable amount of time, make sure the gas flow through
the instrument constant throughout the test.

Once you have obtained a stable dew point reading, use the
chart on the next page to convert your dew point reading to moisture content in
ppm by volume or ppm by weight. With a ruler draw a straight line from 1 bar on
the right column through the point in the center column of your obtained
reading. Extend the line to the left column and read off moisture content of the
gas under test in ppm by volume.

If there is no means of reducing the breaker or GIS compartment
pressure, use the same test hook- up but ignore the pressure reducing valve.
However you will now use the flowmeter valve to control the gas flow throug the
instrument. First open valve (5) all the way, then open the valve (8) on the
flowmeter slightly until you have the desired gas flow of 30 L/H .To obtain a
ppm reading use the chart again but this time start with the exact pressure you
are applying to the ( Gas In ) point of the instrument e.g .3.5 bars or 6.2
bars..

New SF6 gas 
should have a moisture content of approximately 125 PPMv equivalent to 15 PPMg a 
reading of 500 PPMv (62 PPMg) or higher indicates problems the gas should be 
exchanged with a new gas or in case of GIS equipment (a very large quantity of 
gas) it is more economical touse the gas truck to re-condition the gas OR 
(treatment the gas)

Important 
Before test, clean and dry the lines and instrument must be purged for several 
minutes the gas to be tested before the actual test carried out.

For further information on instrument calibration and cleaning
of the internal dew point mirror consult the manufacturers instruction manual .

sections.text: Interpetation of test results

New SF6 gas should have a moisture content of approximately
125 ppmv equivalent to 15 ppmg . A reading of 500 ppmv (62ppmg) or higher
indicates problems. The gas should be exchanged with new gas or in case
of GIS equipment (a very large quantity of gas ) it is more economical to use
the gas truck to re-condition the gas.

Properties of SF6

Sulpher Hexaflouride SF6 as a gas is 
 approximately five times heavier than air and possesses excellent properties. 
 At room temperature and normal pressure (20ºC,1bar) it is gaseous and has 
 adensity of 6.0 89/L its critical temperature is 45.6ºC for ease of 
 transportation and treatment SF6 can be liguified by compressing as apure gas 
 it is colourless, odourless, non-inflammable, non - toxic and inert
Electrical Characteristics

SF6 has excellent dielectric properties.
 The dielectric strength of SF6 gas at 2 bare is more than twice that of air at 
 the same pressure and exceeds that of insulting oil the dielectric strength 
 increases as gas pressure is increased.

sections.text:
Filling the circuit breaker 
 reference 
 to figures no. 3, 4 
 For 
 reference to figures no. 3, 4

This avoids the necessity to evacute the C.B 
 poles on site. consequently after erection it is only necessary to increase 
 the gas pressure in the breaker poles to the rated filling perssure of 6 bar 
 gauge refer to 20 ºC corresponding to the black mark on the green range of the 
 density relay and the filling pressure curve

After completing maintenance the breaker poles 
 are reflled with SF6 gas as follows:

Connecd the vacuum pump with pressure gauge to 
 the filling and start the vacuum in the C.B down to a pressure of 0.133m bar 
 with the pump running continue pumping for a nother 30 minutes then stop the 
 pump and shut it off

Leave for two hours and note the pressure and 
 record

Check the pressure again after at least 10 hours, 
 record the value

Comparing the two values it is possible to 
 determine whether the C.B interrupting chambers are sufficiently

After establishing the C.B to be gastight couple 
 the filling hose of the topping up gas unit

Charge the SF6 gas up to pressure of 6 bar gauge 
 referred to 20 ºC corresponding to the black mark on the green field of the 
 density relay scale

Disconnect the filling hose and screw the cover 
 cap

It is Recommended to leave the manual stop valves 
 open during normal service
